title: sustained-throughput-evaluator-and-elastic-credit-republisher
author: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: This PR introduces a sustained throughput evaluator and an elastic credit republisher to improve burst stability for Dedicated fleets. Motivation: current burst allocation responds to short spikes and can cause oscillation and inefficient reserved utilization when many tenants briefly spike in the same window. The evaluator computes a smoothed sustained throughput estimate per-tenant over a configurable multi-minute window and exposes a confidence score. The republisher periodically reclaims unused elastic credits from tenants that are underutilizing reserved capacity and makes them available to nearby clusters or to a cross-tenant soft-pool for short bursts. The aim is to: 1) reduce oscillatory scale-ups caused by transient spikes, 2) improve utilization of reserved capacity without violating tenant throughput promises, and 3) provide more predictable tail latency during sustained load.

Design: - sustained throughput evaluator: implemented as a sliding-window sampler that computes per-tenant P50/P90 sustained token/sec and a decay-weighted moving average. The evaluator runs as part of the scheduler gateway and emits metrics (sustained_throughput_tokens_per_sec, sustained_confidence_score). It also annotates allocation decisions with a stability flag that downstream allocators can use to prefer soft capacity adjustments over hard reservations. - elastic credit republisher: a background controller that scans tenant ledgers weekly and ephemeral warm-pools each minute; when credits are identified as idle (not consumed for the credit_ttl window) the controller republishes them into a regional soft-pool, tagging with origin tenant id and an expiry. Republished credits can be consumed by other tenants under a fail-safe allocation policy that respects tenant-level SLA watermarks. - Safety and correctness: we added a conservative safety-checker that prevents republishing credits if the tenant has any open canary traffic or pinned reservations. All republished credits are soft (no hard commitment) and are consumed only after the local scheduler verifies low local reservation pressure.

Checklist: - [x] evaluator implementation and unit tests - [x] republisher controller and integration tests - [x] telemetry (metrics + dashboards) - [x] documentation (operators/credit-republisher.md) - [x] e2e smoke test against a small Dedicated cluster

Commits: - 1) add sustained throughput evaluator, sampling and metrics (maya/throughput-evaluator) - 2) implement elastic credit republisher and scheduler hooks (maya/credit-republisher) - 3) add unit tests and e2e smoke harness, update docs and dashboards (maya/tests-and-docs)

Files changed (high level): - pkg/autoscaler/evaluator.go (new) - controllers/credit_republisher.go (new) - controllers/republisher/safety_checker.go (new) - scheduler/allocation_pipeline.go (touched to consume stability flag) - telemetry/metrics.yaml (added new metrics and scrape configs) - docs/operators/credit-republisher.md (new operator guide) - test/e2e/credit_republish_smoke_test.go (new)

Review conversation (high level): - Diego: "The decay constant needs a clearer rationale. Why choose 3 minutes? Can we make this tenant-configurable and add a brief note in the docs? Also please ensure the evaluator doesn't add CPU pressure to the gateway." - Maya: "Made the window configurable via fleet/tenant policy (defaults to 3m). Added a benchmark showing ~12% CPU for 10k tenants at 1s sample rate; lowered internal sample frequency and added jitter." - Priya: "Safety checker looks good; add a unit test for the pinned-reservation case." - Maya: "Added pinned reservation unit test and a new e2e scenario where pinned reservations prevent republish." - Evan: "Telemetry naming and tagging look solid; we'll need dashboards for oncall to catch republished-credit thrash. Can ops have a doc snippet?" - Maya: "Added ops doc and sample dashboard panels in telemetry/README.md."

CI summary: - ci/build: pass - ci/unit: pass (one flaky test flaked on first run: TestWarmPoolExpiry, rerun passed) - ci/e2e-smoke: pass - ci/lint: pass

Performance notes: In cluster-scale benchmarks (10k tenants, varied workloads) sustained estimator reduced spurious autoscaler reservations by ~18% and overall reserved GPU idle time dropped by ~9% vs baseline. End-to-end 99th latency tail remained within SLA for high-load tenants.

Merge: Squash-merged into main after reviewers approved. Merged by Priya Kapoor on 2025-01-24. Rollout: feature gated behind "enable_sustained_evaluator" and "enable_credit_republisher" flags; will be enabled for 10% of fleets initially and monitored for credit churn.
